# Security Posture Register

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build-posture-register.py from posture.yml — do not edit by hand. -->

Every security-relevant setting observed in this environment, its state, and
whether it must be reconsidered before the project is complete.

A lab accumulates weakenings. Each is defensible when made and invisible three
weeks later. This register exists so the final audit is a lookup rather than an
excavation.

## Legend

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| hardened | Set to the secure/recommended value |
| default | Inherited, not chosen — recorded so it is never mistaken for a decision |
| **weakening** | Deliberately loosened for lab convenience; production answer differs |
| **gap** | Should be enabled per vendor guidance or exam scope; currently is not |

**Verified** means the state was observed directly in a portal view. Unverified
entries are assertions, not findings, and are listed separately below.

**`G1`–`G5`** in the notes below refer to the lab's source guides *as originally
written*. All five have since been revised and these divergences folded into them, so
the current versions no longer state what these notes record them as stating. The
originals are not reproducible here. Treat every claim about what a guide said as
testimony rather than something a reader can check.

**`POS-001` — Security Defaults.** Active change, not inherited. Nothing replaced it — no Conditional Access exists, so the tenant runs with no baseline identity protection. Required to be off before Conditional Access can be used at all.

**`POS-002` — Admin identity model.** VERIFIED 2026-08-06, AND NARROWED TO WHAT THE READ SUPPORTS. This entry carried verified: null from 2026-07-16 to 2026-08-06 as the register's sole unverified gap. Closed on a direct portal read: Users > Active users > admin > Account renders Roles: Global Administrator, and the same grid renders labuser as "No administrator access" and analyst as unlicensed with no directory role. Three active member accounts, one of which holds GA, standing - no PIM, no eligibility, no second admin. Corroborated on a second surface the same day (Entra ID > Users > All users, "3 users found", all Member, no guests). NARROWED: the original state line read "across all portals". A single directory role assignment is tenant-wide by construction, so the phrase added nothing a role read could confirm or deny and is dropped rather than left as an unfalsifiable flourish. What is verified is the role, its standing (not eligible) character, and the absence of any alternative admin identity. What is NOT claimed: that every portal was individually exercised with this credential. SCOPE OF THE READ: Active users lists active member accounts. Guests (Users > Guest users) and soft-deleted accounts (Users > Deleted users) are separate views and were not enumerated in the admin center; the Entra cross-check shows guests inline and found none. The claim is therefore "three active accounts, one standing GA", not "three accounts have ever existed". revisit stays TRUE. Verifying a weakening does not remediate it - the entry is now an observed finding rather than an asserted one, and the production answer is unchanged. One credential holds total authority; audit trail cannot distinguish this identity's actions from any other's because there is no other. POS-027 creates a scoped analyst identity for the Defender portal. That does not close this entry and the state above is unchanged: analyst holds one read permission and no directory role, so the admin identity model is still a single standing Global Administrator, and the Global Administrator is still the account doing the work. This closes when the second identity is the one being used, not when it exists. POS-021 recorded the endpoint version of that distinction as closed and POS-024 found it open three days later.

**`POS-003` — Conditional Access policies.** Inferred, not observed. The Manage security defaults control being available is suggestive (the option is hidden where CA is in use) but is not proof. Needs a direct look at the CA blade.

**`POS-004` — Elevate access to all Azure subscriptions.** Governs whether the Global Administrator can assume User Access Administrator across every subscription and management group. At default.

**`POS-005` — Azure subscription funding model.** CORRECTED 2026-08-01 — the original premise is disproven; the conclusion survives on different grounds. As first written (2026-07-16) this entry asserted "free-credit offer unavailable". That was wrong: a $200 Azure sign-up credit EXISTS, effective 2026-07-14, expiring 2026-08-13. It was invisible because it sits on a different billing profile than the one carrying lab spend (POS-058) — the surface consulted was resource cost, which answers a different question than the payment-methods page. What survives, and is now worse than either position previously held: the spending limit feature is unavailable on subscriptions with pay-as-you-go pricing, so this environment has credit WITHOUT the "services disabled, never charged" safety net the credit model normally implies. There is still no mechanism that stops spend — only ones that report it. Deallocating lab compute remains the primary cost control (with the POS-016 correction: compute only), and the budget is what reports that the habit slipped. A gap entry that was accidentally right.

**`POS-015` — Cost budgets - two, at different scopes.** Two budgets exist deliberately rather than one. The resource-group budget (Defender-Lab-Budget, $40) is the tighter tripwire on the lab's own resources; the subscription budget (Subscription-Lab-Budget, $50) is the backstop that catches spend the first one structurally cannot see. The subscription amount is kept ABOVE the resource-group amount on purpose, so the RG tripwire alerts before the subscription backstop — inverting them (backstop below tripwire) would make the wider budget fire first and defeat the tiering. Consolidating to one was rejected in both directions: a resource-group budget cannot see spend outside its group — which matters once Lab 04 creates the Log Analytics workspace, since ingestion is the largest projected cost and may not land there — and a subscription budget cannot attribute spend to a component. Cost of keeping both is duplicate mail when spend falls inside the group. Budget scope is fixed at creation, so the subscription budget had to be created new rather than rescoped. LIMITS, recorded rather than assumed away: (1) Azure budgets notify, they do not cap. There is no spending limit on pay-as-you-go, so spend continues past 100 percent. POS-016 — deallocating the VM — remains the only actual control; the budget only reports that the habit slipped. (2) Azure evaluates budgets roughly every 8-24 hours, not on demand, so an alert can arrive a day after a runaway resource starts billing. (3) These budgets cover Azure consumption ONLY. The Microsoft 365 E5 conversion (POS-017) bills through a separate system and is invisible to Azure Cost Management at any scope. The most certain charge on this tenant has no alert attached to it — only a calendar date. (4) Both budgets now carry forecasted alerting (actual 50/80/100 + forecasted 100). An earlier state had the resource-group budget as actual-only; on the 2026-07-19 raise it was confirmed to include a forecasted-100 alert, so both give forward warning rather than only after-the-fact. (5) Notification path VALIDATED 2026-07-19: the resource-group budget's 50-percent and forecasted alerts fired at ~50 percent of the old $15 amount and the configured recipients received the mail. This upgrades the earlier state, where no alert had ever fired and the path was recorded as an unvalidated hypothesis. The alerting is now a confirmed control, not an assumption. (Recipient addresses are held in the portal only and are not recorded here.)

**`POS-016` — Lab VM power state discipline.** Portal status column reads "Stopped (deallocated)", not "Stopped". Compute is released and not billing. The distinction is load-bearing rather than pedantic: shutting down from inside the guest OS leaves the VM allocated and billing, and the portal reports that state as plain "Stopped". This is the primary cost control on this subscription. POS-005 records that pay-as-you-go has no spending limit, and POS-015 records that Azure budgets notify but do not cap and are evaluated only every 8-24 hours. CORRECTED 2026-08-01 — as first written this note called deallocation "the only mechanism here that actually ends spend". That is true for COMPUTE and false as a general claim: managed disks and public IP addresses bill while they exist, and both continued accruing into August with both VMs deallocated. The July invoice measured the gap — ~$10.84 pre-tax actual against ~$7.58 tracked, an understatement of roughly 43%, most of it storage and IP hours attributed to "deallocated" machines. Deallocation ends compute spend; only deletion ends resource spend. The same shape as Bastion (billed while existing, no stopped state), now measured on resources that DO have a stopped state — the stopped state just covers less than the word suggests. REVISIT: verified as a one-time observation, not as a control. The current mechanism is operator memory, which is not a control at all — Lab 03 onward introduces sessions that end at whatever time they end. An auto-shutdown schedule (VM > Operations > Auto-shutdown) would make it one, and would cost nothing. Left open deliberately rather than closed on the strength of a habit.

**`POS-017` — M365 trial recurring billing.** Two subscriptions exist. Office 365 E5 was the acquisition path — the operator reports it had to be signed up for before Microsoft 365 E5 could be added — and each carries its own recurring billing setting, so turning one off does nothing for the other. Both are configured 1 license, 1 month, pay monthly: O365 E5 at $49.20/mo, M365 E5 rate not yet displayed while in trial. Left alone, BOTH would have converted on 2026-08-13 - the state as first recorded 2026-07-16, before O365's recurring billing was turned off and before the M365 extension moved its conversion to 2026-09-15. Microsoft 365 E5 is a superset of Office 365 E5 and is the license actually assigned to the admin account, so O365 E5 contributes nothing operationally. Its recurring billing was turned OFF on 2026-07-16 and verified: the panel now reads "Expires on August 14, 2026" in place of "changes to paid subscription", which is the documented indication that recurring billing is off. Turning it off did not cancel — the trial still runs its full term. CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — THIS ENTRY READ THE WRONG FIELD AS AN EXPIRY DATE. From 2026-07-16 to 2026-08-06 the state line above read "O365 E5 recurring OFF (expires 2026-08-14)". It does not expire on the 14th. The Office 365 E5 product page carries THREE banners and an Expiration date field all reading 2026-08-13; the only surface saying August 14 is the Recurring billing field itself. That field renders the TRANSITION day - the day the consequence of the recurring-billing setting lands - not the trial end. Mechanism labelled as inference; what is observed is that recurring-OFF renders "Expires on August 14" and recurring-ON renders "changes to paid subscription on August 14" in the same slot, both one day after a shared 2026-08-13 expiry. Corroborated by Next invoice available, which reads a date on the recurring-ON subscription and "Date not available" on the recurring-OFF one. See POS-078 for the full cross-surface date spread; this correction is one instance of it. Microsoft 365 E5 recurring billing remains ON deliberately. The trial was EXTENDED on 2026-08-06 (POS-077): expiry moved 2026-08-13 to 2026-09-14 and conversion moved 2026-08-14 to 2026-09-15, still at 1 license, 1 month, pay monthly unless turned off. That is a decision point, not a deadline: month-to-month is cancellable at any renewal, so the lab need not be compressed to fit the trial window. O365 E5 WAS NOT EXTENDED, deliberately. It still lapses 2026-08-13, which leaves the dependency question below testable in isolation rather than simultaneously with a conversion event. SURFACE DISAGREEMENT, recorded 2026-08-01 because stating only the resolution caused a misreading: THREE surfaces report 25 licenses (the trial allocation, the Change plan panel, and the Azure billing inventory) against ONE reporting 1 paid license (the M365 admin center renewal field). The renewal field is the surface that answers "what converts to paid" — 1 license, 1 month, pay monthly — and the 25 is the trial's provisioned allocation, not a purchase commitment. This register originally stated the 1-license answer flatly, which is why the 25 was briefly read as a 25-license billing exposure when re-encountered on another surface. The disagreement is the durable fact; the resolution is one surface's answer to one question. RE-READ 2026-08-06, THIRTEEN DAYS ON, UNCHANGED — and now on four surfaces rather than one. The 1-license answer was found on: the Renew or cancel panel ("bought on August 14, 2026 with 1 licenses"), the Your products grid ("Renews on 8/13/2026 with 1 paid license"), and - new after the extension - a Paid subscription panel that appeared on the product page itself stating Licenses 1, Subscription length 1 month, Billing frequency Pay monthly. That panel sits on the same page as "Your trial of this product includes only 25 licenses" and "2 / 25 Licenses assigned". The disagreement did not resolve; it became legible on one screen. UNVERIFIED, AND TESTED LIVE ON 2026-08-13: whether Microsoft 365 E5 survives Office 365 E5 lapsing. If O365 E5 was structurally required to obtain M365 E5, it may or may not be required to retain it. An acquisition path is not normally an ongoing dependency and M365 E5 is a standalone SKU, so this is expected to be a non-event — but that is a vendor expectation, not an observation, and the distinction is the whole point of this register. Mitigation is free: recurring billing can be turned back on at any point before 2026-08-13 if M365 E5 shows any sign of depending on it. WHAT THE 2026-08-13 TEST NOW COSTS, re-assessed 2026-08-06: nothing that matters. Verified the same day that admin is the ONLY holder of an O365 E5 licence (1/25 assigned) and also holds M365 E5, while labuser holds M365 E5 alone and analyst is unlicensed. No mailbox, OneDrive, or workload in this lab is provisioned by the lapsing subscription - every Office 365 workload exercised in labs 09 and 12-16 is also carried by M365 E5. The lapse is therefore a clean dependency test rather than a capability risk.

**`POS-026` — Defender unified RBAC activation.** The guide states that unified RBAC is the default permissions model for new tenants: Defender for Endpoint since 2025, Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 since July 2026. This tenant was created 2026-07-14, after both. Zero workloads were active. "Default permissions model" means the legacy model is not available to this tenant. It does not mean the unified model is switched on. Those two sentences read the same and are not the same, and the difference is that nothing enforces a role until a workload is activated. Observed directly, and this is the part that will not be reproducible again: the role was created, assigned, and rendered on the Review and finish page as complete. No banner, no warning, no indication that it would not take effect. Signed in as the assigned user before activation - no Incidents, no Hunting, no Assets. Activated the workloads. Signed in again - all three present. Nothing else changed in between. Third instance of this shape in this environment, and the first one a source guide called in advance: POS-011 (connector reads Available, device risk never reaches compliance), POS-022 (every precondition verified, enrolment never attempted), and this. The guide says "the role appears complete without it" and it is correct. The portal does not say it. The before/after was measured on a tenant with no telemetry, which is the only state in which the absence of data proves anything. Onboarding ends that.

**`POS-027` — Defender portal analyst identity and role scope.** Created so that Defender portal work stops requiring the Global Administrator. It does not replace it yet - see POS-002. Deliberately minimal: no directory roles, no group memberships, usage location set at creation because a licence cannot be assigned without one and the failure does not say so. Not given Virtual Machine User Login, and not given labuser's role either. Coupling the SOC console to the endpoint sign-in identity would mean that compromising the box under investigation hands over the console it is investigated from - POS-021's own Primary Refresh Token argument, pointed the other way. No licence was assigned, and none was needed. analyst reached the Defender portal and, after POS-026's activation, the views the role grants. The guide's prerequisites table covers what is required to create a role and says nothing about what the assignee needs; this is the answer it does not give. Scope is wider than it should be. The assignment covers Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, and Cloud Apps - all four - where this lab has endpoints and nothing else. The guide is explicit that data sources are a hard boundary and that scoping to a single workload is done by deselecting the others. The tighter choice was Defender for Endpoint alone, and the wide default was accepted rather than chosen. Recorded as the weaker of two available options, taken by inattention. "Include future data sources automatically" was left unchecked, which is the same class of decision made correctly. Two observations about the portal, neither pursued: analyst reaches the Cloud Discovery landing page - which the assignment's data sources explain - and that page presents "Create a new report" and "Configure automatic upload", write controls offered to an account holding one read permission. Whether they fail on click is untested. Separately, role membership is legible only by opening the Edit assignment dialog; the Roles page reports a count and no names, and unified RBAC is the only store for these assignments, so there is no second surface to check. The only way to audit who holds a Defender role is to open the form that changes it.

**`POS-058` — Azure billing topology - credit placement across billing profiles.** Under a Microsoft Customer Agreement, credits attach to a billing profile and pay down only that profile's invoice. The $200 credit is therefore structurally unable to reach the lab's spend — not expired, not consumed, not conditional: attached to an invoice the lab does not bill to. This is the mechanism behind the POS-005 correction, and it is why the credit was invisible for 18 days — the surface consulted (resource cost analysis) is scoped to the subscription, which belongs to profile B, and profile A's credit appears on no surface reachable from there. DECISION, recorded with reasoning: do not chase the credit. Migrating existing resources or rebuilding state to capture $200 costs hours of an 11-day budget, and the VMs carry ASR state that POS-031's pending enforcement-scope test is a test OF. The credit expires unspent on 2026-08-13 by choice. RE-EXAMINED 2026-08-06 - DECISION STANDS, ITS PRIMARY REASON DOES NOT. The M365 E5 trial extension (POS-077) moved the project clock to 2026-09-14, so the "11-day budget" that made rebuilding unaffordable no longer describes the schedule. THE CREDIT'S OWN DATE DID NOT MOVE: it is an Azure MCA artifact on billing profile A, structurally unrelated to a Microsoft 365 trial, and still expires 2026-08-13 - now SEVEN days out rather than the extended horizon. The decision is unchanged and the remaining reasons are sufficient on their own: the credit still cannot reach profile B's invoice without migration, and the VMs still carry the ASR state POS-031 tests. Recorded because a decision whose stated reason has expired is a decision that will be re-litigated by the next reader if the change is not written down. RELATED HAZARD: the two subscriptions are BOTH named "Azure subscription 1". Every subscription picker in every portal shows the name, and the name does not disambiguate — a deployment aimed at the wrong one would look correct at every step. Renaming one is a standing recommendation, unexecuted because every existing artifact references the current names' GUIDs rather than display names.

**`POS-077` — Microsoft 365 E5 trial extension (one-time, consumed).** Taken deliberately to remove schedule pressure from the remaining work (G57 playbooks and the section-7 queue), not to avoid cost - the conversion was already configured at 1 licence, month-to-month, and cancellable at any renewal. PREDICTION P77-1, recorded before clicking: one 30-day extension, once only, no payment method demanded, no choice of duration, 25-licence allocation unchanged, resulting expiry 2026-09-12 (8/13 + 30). OUTCOME: five of six correct, and the arithmetic wrong. The dialog states verbatim that the trial can be extended once, for 30 days, and that the licences extended today associate with the Microsoft 365 E5 created 7/14/2026. No card, no duration picker, allocation still 25 (2 assigned). But the resulting Expiration date reads 2026-09-14 - THIRTY-TWO days after the previous expiry, not thirty. Nor is it thirty days from the extension date (that would be 2026-09-05). The anchor is not identified and is NOT asserted here; what is observed is a dialog promising 30 and a field moving 32. WHAT PROPAGATED AND WHAT DID NOT. Expiration (8/13 to 9/14) and the Recurring billing conversion line (8/14 to 9/15) both moved by exactly 32 days, preserving the +1 offset intact - so those two fields are a derived pair, not independent values, which is a useful negative result for POS-078. Next invoice available did NOT move: it still reads 8/15/2026, now thirty days BEFORE the paid subscription it invoices for begins. A stale field with no indication that it is stale, on the same panel as the two that updated correctly. EXTENSION CONSUMED - verified by observation, not by the dialog's claim. The Extend trial end date control renders greyed and inert after the operation. The dialog said once-only; the control's state is what confirms it. There is no second extension available, so 2026-09-14 is a hard floor. ASYNCHRONOUS WRITE. Confirmation was two-stage - "Your request is being verified" then "Your request is accepted and pending processing. It will be processed within a minute." The confirmation confirms RECEIPT, not EFFECT; the product page had to be refreshed before any field moved. A read taken immediately after the click would have shown the old dates and proved nothing. Same shape as every other propagation delay in this repo. revisit TRUE: the stale invoice date should be re-read closer to 2026-09-15 to see whether it self-corrects or persists to the actual first invoice.

**`POS-078` — Trial expiry and conversion dates disagree across portal surfaces.** Captured in one sitting on 2026-08-06, pre-extension, all five surfaces inside admin.microsoft.com and all describing the same pair of trials. 8/12 - Users > Active users > admin > Licences and apps, banner: the Office 365 E5 trial expires on 8/12/2026. 8/13 - Office 365 E5 product page: three separate banners plus the Expiration date field. Also Billing > Your products for O365 E5. Also Your products for M365 E5, worded "Renews on 8/13/2026 with 1 paid licence". 8/14 - Microsoft 365 E5 product page Recurring billing line ("changes to paid subscription on August 14, 2026") and the Renew or cancel panel ("bought on August 14, 2026"). Also the O365 E5 Recurring billing line, worded "Expires on August 14, 2026". 8/15 - Microsoft 365 E5 product page, Next invoice available. A fifth datum constrains it: the Extend trial dialog states the M365 E5 was created 7/14/2026, and 30 days from creation is 8/13 - arithmetically consistent with the Expiration fields and inconsistent with both the 8/12 banner and the 8/14 conversion language. MECHANISM PARTLY IDENTIFIED, PARTLY NOT. The 8/13-vs-8/14 pair is explained: expiry and conversion are consecutive by construction, and POS-077 confirmed it by moving both 32 days with the offset preserved. 8/15 is invoice availability, a third real event. 8/12 is NOT explained and is not guessed at - it is the earliest date any Microsoft surface claims for a trial ending, it appears on exactly one surface, and it was read once. Recorded as unresolved. WHY THIS IS AN ENTRY AND NOT A FOOTNOTE. Three of the four dates describe genuinely different events (expiry, conversion, invoice) that a reader naturally collapses into "when does the trial end". The register itself collapsed two of them for three weeks - see the correction inside POS-017, where the Recurring billing field's transition day was recorded as the O365 expiry date. The repo's recurring instruction applies exactly: identify which question a surface answers before trusting its number.

**`POS-079` — Licence inventory differs by surface - no surface lists all SKUs.** Verified 2026-08-06 across three surfaces in one sitting. Users > Active users, Licences column and its filter dropdown: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Power Automate Free, Office 365 E5. Billing > Your products (3 items): Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Entra ID Free, Office 365 E5. Billing > Licences > Subscriptions (2 items): Microsoft 365 E5, Office 365 E5. Power Automate Free appears only where licences are assigned to people. Entra ID Free appears only where products are billed. The Licences page - whose stated job is licence inventory - shows the fewest of the three. TWO-READ RULE APPLIED, AND IT MATTERED. Power Automate Free was first seen once, in the Active users grid, and the working hypothesis was that the grid was stale. The confirming read (admin > Licences and apps) returned it CHECKED, with "9999 of 10000 licences available" - a real 10,000-seat SKU with one seat consumed. So the assignment is genuine and the billing surfaces are the ones omitting it. Had the finding been written from the single read it would have pointed the wrong way. TWO HYPOTHESES WITHDRAWN in reaching this. (1) The Your products filter chip reading "Subscription status: Active, Pending, Scheduled, +2" was called a pre-seeded filter hiding rows - Reset all changed nothing and the Add filter panel renders Subscription status and Billing profile greyed, i.e. it is the default inclusive view. (2) Billing > Licences was predicted to surface the SKU because its own filter reads "Account type: Organization, Self-service" - self-service SKUs are explicitly in scope there and it still is not listed. Both were inference, both disproven by reading. NOT CHASED, recorded as open: the Licences page carries Requests and Auto-claim policy tabs, neither examined. Whether tenant self-service sign-up is enabled remains unanswered - see POS-080.

**`POS-080` — Two SKUs present in the tenant that this register never recorded.** Recorded as kind default precisely because neither was a decision. Both surfaced only during the 2026-08-06 licensing audit, after eighteen labs. POWER AUTOMATE FREE - assigned to admin, checkbox confirmed on the Licences and apps tab. How it arrived is NOT established. The working hypothesis is self-service auto-provisioning on first contact with a Power Platform surface, which would mean tenant self-service sign-up is enabled and any licensed user can provision SKUs without an admin - a posture setting in its own right. That hypothesis is UNTESTED: the field that would answer it (Purchase channel) is on the Your products page, and Power Automate Free is not listed there (POS-079). Not asserted. ENTRA ID FREE - Purchased quantity 1, Purchase channel Commercial direct, Product type License-based, and Pricing model PAID on a SKU whose name is Free. Assigned licences reads "Not available". Almost certainly the baseline directory SKU every tenant carries, surfaced by the billing view rather than provisioned by anyone; the Paid pricing model on a free product is unexplained and not explained away here. NO COST EXPOSURE at lab volume for either, and neither bears on G57: Sentinel playbooks bill as Logic Apps consumption, a different meter from Power Automate. WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY. The register's purpose is that inherited state is recorded so it is not later mistaken for a decision. Two SKUs sat in this tenant for over three weeks, one of them assigned to the account that operates every lab, and the register had no entry for either. They were found by auditing licensing for an unrelated reason.

| `POS-025` | VM local administrator account | `Azure > (VM) > Run command; Get-LocalUser, net accounts, secedit` | labadmin, enabled, is the built-in Administrator renamed (RID 500), password does not expire | default | yes | 2026-07-17 |

**`POS-006` — Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra ID.** Observed in the portal 2026-07-19: Entra join and registration settings show "Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra = All", Selected empty — the asserted value confirmed, not merely recorded on the operator's word. Device identity is an authentication surface. Set to All, any credential — including a compromised one — can register an attacker-controlled device into the directory.

**`POS-018` — VM Security Type.** Instructed by G5, which says to change Security Type to Standard without stating what that costs. Observed at four independent layers rather than inferred from one: the VM JSON has no securityProfile block; Get-Tpm reports TpmPresent False and TpmReady False; Confirm-SecureBootUEFI returns False; and dsregcmd reports TpmProtected NO with KeyProvider "Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider". Two consequences the guide does not mention. First, the device's Entra identity key is software-protected on disk rather than sealed in hardware. The Entra sign-in log independently records "Token protection - Sign In Session: Unbound (Status code: 1003)": with no vTPM the Primary Refresh Token cannot be bound to the device, so a stolen token is replayable elsewhere. That is the same fact surfacing in the identity plane. Second, Intune compliance policies commonly evaluate Secure Boot and TPM. This device cannot satisfy either. So the risk-to-compliance chain is broken in two independent places — POS-011 blocks the signal, and this entry means the device would fail the checks even if the signal arrived. Fixing POS-011 alone would not produce a working control.

**`POS-019` — RDP inbound exposure (NSG).** G5 instructs "Ensure RDP (3389) is allowed" and the portal default source is Any, which means the entire internet. Azure VMs with 3389 open to Any are found by opportunistic scanners within minutes of the public IP becoming live. Not in source guidance; changed to "My IP address" on 2026-07-17. The exposure was never RDP alone — it was the composition. Open 3389, plus NLA disabled (POS-020) removing pre-authentication, plus no MFA baseline (POS-001), plus no Conditional Access (POS-003), plus a standing Global Administrator as the sign-in identity (POS-002), is an internet-facing path to tenant compromise. Each element is individually defensible in a lab. Together they are not, and no single guide step is wrong enough to notice. The VM being deallocated between sessions is what kept this theoretical. Residential source IP rotates; the rule needs updating when it does. Symptom is an RDP timeout rather than an error.

**`POS-020` — Network Level Authentication.** Instructed by G5, and genuinely required for its approach: Entra ID authentication happens at the Windows login screen, and NLA forces credential validation before a session exists, so NLA blocks the flow. Verified at both ends independently. Server side: registry UserAuthentication = 0, read via Azure Run command without opening an RDP session — the exposed path was not used to inspect the exposed path. Client side: the .rdp file carries enablecredsspsupport:i:0. The .rdp file weakens two things, and G5 explains one. It also sets "authentication level:i:2", which means warn-but-connect when server identity cannot be verified — a downgrade of server authentication, not just of client pre-authentication. Unmentioned in the guide. With NLA off, the pre-authentication attack surface is exposed to anything that can reach 3389. That was the entire internet until POS-019 was scoped.

**`POS-021` — Endpoint sign-in identity.** Not in source guidance. G5 signs into the VM as the tenant Global Administrator, because at that point in the course it is the only Entra account that exists. That matters more than it appears. When an Entra-joined device authenticates a user, it receives a Primary Refresh Token for that account and the token lives on the device. Signing in as Global Admin places a tenant-admin token on the endpoint that later labs deliberately attack. Combined with POS-018 (no vTPM, so the PRT is unbound and replayable), compromising the box would mean compromising the tenant. Created labuser: no directory roles, no group memberships, Microsoft 365 E5 assigned (required — an unlicensed account will not enrol), and Virtual Machine User Login rather than Administrator Login, scoped to the single VM resource. The Global Administrator no longer touches the endpoint — as a practice. The capability survived: POS-024 records the Virtual Machine Administrator Login assignment that G5 created and this change never removed. This entry is a real hardening of which account is used. It is not a hardening of which accounts can be used, and it read as one until POS-024 was looked for. This is also more faithful for the labs that follow: ASR and attack-simulation results taken as a non-admin reflect what a real analyst would see.

**`POS-022` — Intune automatic MDM enrolment.** THE LAB 01 FINDING. G2, as originally written, stated that on sign-in the device registers with Entra and then silently registers with Intune. It does not. The device joined Entra on 2026-07-14 and was still absent from Intune three days later. Every precondition was verified individually, and all of them pass: - MDM user scope = All (Entra portal, POS-007) - device holds the correct MDM discovery URL (dsregcmd Tenant Details, matching the portal value exactly — the setting confirmed from both ends independently) - DeviceEligible : YES (dsregcmd Ngc Prerequisite Check) - AzureAdPrt : YES, acquired 2026-07-17 17:09:30 UTC And nothing happens: - no scheduled tasks under \Microsoft\Windows\EnterpriseMgmt - no enrolment events (ID 71/72/75/76) anywhere in the DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider/Admin log, which spans back before the VM existed - device absent from Intune Not blocked. Never started. No error is raised because nothing is attempted. The likely cause is the join path. G5 builds an Azure VM whose Entra join is performed by the AADLoginForWindows extension at deployment, not by a user-driven join through Settings or OOBE. MDM user scope is necessary but not sufficient — something must trigger enrolment, and the extension join appears not to. Suggestive but not proven: Azure Virtual Desktop host-pool creation offers an explicit "enrol VMs with Intune" checkbox that plain VM creation does not, which would be unnecessary if extension joins enrolled by themselves. Stated as a hypothesis rather than a conclusion. What is established is the observation: preconditions met, behaviour absent, silent. G2 and G5 are each internally correct. G2 describes user-driven join behaviour; G5 builds a VM that does not join that way. Followed together they produce a device that will never enrol, and neither guide is wrong enough for the failure to surface. Left unenrolled deliberately. Lab 03 onboards to Defender via local script and does not require Intune. Forcing enrolment (deviceenroller.exe /c /AutoEnrollMDM) requires local administrator, which POS-021 deliberately removed, and it enrols in the calling user's context — so forcing it as Global Admin would bind the device to the account POS-021 exists to keep off the endpoint.

**`POS-023` — VM auto-shutdown schedule.** Instructed by G5 as part of deployment. This is what closes POS-016's open item: deallocation was previously a habit, and a habit is not a control. Notification before shutdown was configured beyond what the guide specifies. Load-bearing because of POS-005 and POS-015: pay-as-you-go has no spending limit, and budgets notify but do not cap and are only evaluated every 8-24 hours. This schedule is the only mechanism in the environment that ends spend without a human deciding to.

**`POS-024` — Global Administrator interactive login rights on the lab endpoint.** Instructed by G5 section 2, which assigns Virtual Machine Administrator Login to "your administrator account" — at that point in the course the Global Administrator is the only Entra account that exists, so the guide is correct for its own sequence. It was never revisited afterwards. POS-021 created labuser with Virtual Machine User Login and recorded that the Global Administrator no longer touches the endpoint. That was true of the practice and not of the configuration. This assignment was never removed, so the tenant Global Administrator can open an interactive RDP session on the lab endpoint as a local administrator, today. The distinction is the finding: POS-021 changed which account is used, not which accounts can be used. Nothing in the portal reports the gap. The IAM blade lists both assignments side by side and raises nothing, because both are valid — the same shape as POS-009 reading Available while POS-011 is off. Compounds with POS-018 and POS-020. No vTPM means a PRT minted on this device is unbound and replayable; NLA is disabled, so the pre-auth lock screen is reachable by anything that can reach 3389. POS-019 scoped that to a single address, and that scoping is currently what carries the weight of this entry. Not yet removed, and removal is now known to be free: POS-025 records labadmin, which administers this endpoint with no Entra role at all. The scope of this entry is the open part. Local Administrators also holds two Entra-backed SIDs put there by the device join itself, independent of any RBAC assignment. If either is the Global Administrator directory role, then removing this assignment closes nothing and this entry names the wrong mechanism. Unresolved — resolving it costs either an enterprise-app consent or a Cloud Shell storage account, neither of which is on the path to Lab 03. Recorded as a prediction with a date on it, not a conclusion.

**`POS-025` — VM local administrator account.** Instructed by G5 section 1 step 4 — "Administrator Account: Enter a username and a secure password. Write down this password" — and used in section 3 to RDP in and turn NLA off. It was never recorded here until POS-024 forced the question of what else could administer this box. labadmin is not a new account. Its SID ends -500, so it is the built-in Administrator, renamed by Azure provisioning. That is why Get-LocalUser lists four accounts and none of them is called Administrator, and it is why "I created labadmin at provisioning" and "labadmin is the built-in" are the same fact rather than competing ones. The rename buys nothing against anyone enumerating SIDs: the RID is the identifier and the name is decoration. The password does not expire. Local policy sets maximum password age to 42 days; the account carries the never-expires flag Azure sets at provisioning, and the flag wins. Two settings disagree, both are visible only from the device, and neither surface mentions the other. Lockout does apply, and this was verified rather than assumed: AllowAdministratorLockout = 1 in the effective policy, so RID 500 is not exempt the way it was before Windows 11 22H2. Threshold 10, duration 10 minutes, observation window 10 minutes. That throttles an attempt against the pre-auth lock screen POS-020 leaves reachable; it does not stop one. POS-019's source scoping is what carries this entry, not the lockout. Also default, also unhardened, recorded because "nobody changed it" is a state: minimum password length 0, password history none, minimum password age 0.

**`POS-009` — Microsoft Intune connection (Defender side).** Connection status reads Available from the Intune side.

**`POS-010` — Allow MDE to enforce Endpoint Security Configurations.** This is Security Settings Management — it governs MDE enforcing configuration on devices onboarded to MDE but NOT enrolled in Intune. Lab devices are expected to be Intune-enrolled, so this toggle does not serve the scenario being built. Harmless, but not load-bearing here.

**`POS-011` — Connect Windows devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.** The toggle that makes Intune compliance policies include MDE risk signals (threat detections, risk scores) when evaluating the device threat level rule. Off means the connection is Available but device risk does NOT reach compliance for Windows — the risk > compliance > Conditional Access chain is architecture, not a working control. Vendor guidance sets this On.

**`POS-012` — Connect Android / iOS devices to MDE (compliance + app protection).** No mobile devices in this lab. Out of scope rather than missing.

### Lab 03

| ID | Setting | Location | State | Kind | Revisit | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POS-028` | VM guest-agent extension channel | `Azure > (VM) > Run command / VMAccess; guest agent status` | Guest agent reports Ready (2.7.41491.1216); Run Command and VMAccess extension operations accept and then hang without completing | **gap** | yes | 2026-07-18 |
| `POS-029` | Endpoint sensor (Defender for Endpoint onboarding) | `security.microsoft.com > Assets > Devices; DeviceInfo` | LAB-WIN11-01 onboarded, sensor Active, streaming; ConnectivityType Streamlined; onboarded via local script | hardened | yes | 2026-07-18 |
| `POS-042` | Defender XDR email notification rules (Incidents / Actions / Threat analytics) | `Defender portal > Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Email notifications` | No rules on any of the three tabs. Observed 2026-07-27, not changed. | **gap** | yes | 2026-07-27 |

**`POS-028` — VM guest-agent extension channel.** Found while onboarding. The intended onboarding method was the local script executed as SYSTEM via Azure Run Command, chosen to keep an interactive privileged session off the endpoint (POS-021). Run Command accepted the script and never returned. A later password-reset via the VMAccess extension behaved identically: the control plane reported the operation InProgress and looped indefinitely without completing. Meanwhile control-plane reads about the VM returned instantly, and the guest agent reported Ready, version 2.7.41491.1216. So the agent is up for status but not executing extensions. "Ready" is not evidence the extension channel works — the same shape as POS-011's "Available" and POS-026's role that "appears complete". A status field answered a narrower question than the one being asked. Consequence for Lab 03: the SYSTEM elevation path was unavailable, forcing the interactive labadmin route via Azure Bastion. That is the divergence recorded in the Lab 03 design decisions and the configuration-inventory divergence table — intended SYSTEM, forced to the RID-500 local admin (POS-025) that the VM design otherwise routes around. Not diagnosed to root cause. May clear on an agent restart or VM redeploy; neither attempted, because the interactive path completed the lab. Left open deliberately: a VM whose extension channel is wedged is a real state and worth confirming persists before treating it as resolved.

**`POS-029` — Endpoint sensor (Defender for Endpoint onboarding).** The SOC's first endpoint. Before this the Device* advanced-hunting tables were empty; after it they are the data plane later labs read from. Onboarded by local script because the scalable Intune path (module 26) is structurally foreclosed here: it requires an Intune-enrolled device, and POS-022 records that enrolment never fires. Even were that fixed, the device-risk-to-compliance path is independently off (POS-011) and the VM cannot attest (POS-018, no vTPM). Three independent breaks; local script is the only available path. Measured latencies, all normalised to UTC and all at or under the vendor numbers: onboard to device-in-inventory ~2 min (vendor 5-30 min); onboard to first telemetry ingested ~3.5 min (FirstEvent 08:30:16Z, FirstIngest 08:33:52Z); detection test to alert ~2 min (vendor "a few minutes"). These measured numbers are the finding; the vendor ranges are recorded only for comparison. Connectivity type Streamlined, chosen at download and confirmed applied via DeviceInfo.ConnectivityType rather than assumed from the selection. The device is now watched but not governed - it emits telemetry and obeys no policy, because onboarding is telemetry and enrolment (the management path) never completed. An analyst inheriting this environment sees a fully reporting endpoint and could assume it is managed. It is not. That gap is the whole point of keeping onboarding and enrolment as separate entries.

**`POS-042` — Defender XDR email notification rules (Incidents / Actions / Threat analytics).** Observed 2026-07-27 during module 55, read-only, nothing changed. Defender XDR > Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Email notifications carries three tabs - Incidents, Actions, and Threat analytics. ALL THREE ARE EMPTY. No notification rule of any kind has ever existed in this tenant. So nobody is emailed when an incident is created, when a remediation action needs approval, or when a threat relevant to this tenant is published. This is the shipped default across all three, not a decision. Two things make it concrete rather than theoretical. Lab 03 produced a real incident on 2026-07-18 and nothing told anyone - it sat in the queue until someone happened to look. And the Action center guidance states that pending actions hold up the automated investigation until they are resolved, while nothing would announce that there are any to resolve. THE CONTRAST WORTH KEEPING: the Azure budget notification path in this same project is VERIFIED WORKING - an alert fired and was received. The cost control notifies. The security controls do not. Same tenant, same operator, opposite outcomes, and both by default rather than by decision. This is the seventh inherited silent default recorded across four feature areas, after positive reinforcement, confirm-before-reporting, success message and results email (POS-038, POS-040). Every one is a communication path that exists and is switched off. The pattern is now large enough to be the finding: Microsoft ships the security consoles quiet, and a tenant that has configured nothing will be told nothing. Not enabled here. Turning it on would need a recipient address, and this project keeps addresses out of the repository; the state is recorded as inherited rather than corrected. In production this is among the first things to configure, because every other control in this register is worthless if no one is told it fired.

### Lab 04

| ID | Setting | Location | State | Kind | Revisit | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POS-032` | Microsoft Sentinel workspace and Defender XDR ingestion | `Azure > Log Analytics workspace law-lab-01; Microsoft Sentinel; Data connectors` | Sentinel enabled on law-lab-01 (West US, PAYG). Defender XDR connector Connected/Primary, forwarding incidents and alerts only. Raw Device* event streaming OFF. | hardened | yes | 2026-07-19 |

**`POS-032` — Microsoft Sentinel workspace and Defender XDR ingestion.** The section capstone - the aggregation layer over every prior lab. Endpoint (Lab 03 sensor) to Defender to XDR to Sentinel, proven with a live detection test: a SecurityIncident arrived carrying ProviderName Microsoft XDR, the proof it came through the connector. Defender-to-Sentinel sync measured at ~2 minutes (UTC-converted; the local-vs-UTC timestamp trap applies a fifth time). Cost-safe by design and verified. Ingestion is the only meaningful Sentinel cost and it is volume-based. Only the free alert/incident sync is enabled; raw Device* event streaming is OFF, confirmed by DeviceEvents failing to resolve as a table in the Sentinel Logs blade (it resolves fine in Defender Advanced Hunting - different store). The trial (2026-07-19 to 2026-08-19) covers 10 GB/day on both Sentinel and Log Analytics; the conservative connector keeps usage far under that. Architecture recorded in Lab 04 for reuse: a sensor produces telemetry (on-device, the source), a connector moves it (cloud-to-cloud, no software); Defender Advanced Hunting and Sentinel Logs both speak KQL but query different stores (Defender's free raw lake with column Timestamp vs the billed Log Analytics workspace with column TimeGenerated holding only forwarded data). The project's existing kql/ queries are portable across both - language transfers, store and cost change. Two behaviours worth remembering: the Defender XDR connector is forward-only (historical incidents do not backfill - prove flow with a fresh event); and the incident wrapper (SecurityIncident) syncs ahead of the discrete SecurityAlert, so query SecurityIncident or search * to confirm flow, not SecurityAlert alone. Permissions note: subscription Owner was required for auto-onboard - Global Administrator (a directory role) is not Azure RBAC (POS-024).

### Lab 05

| ID | Setting | Location | State | Kind | Revisit | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POS-030` | Device group, automation level, and scoped delegation | `security.microsoft.com > Settings > Endpoints > Permissions > Device groups` | Group "Lab Client Machines", rule Name starts-with the lab prefix, remediation Semi (approval required for non-temporary folders), user access scoped to an Entra group holding the analyst identity | hardened | yes | 2026-07-19 |

**`POS-030` — Device group, automation level, and scoped delegation.** Two boundaries in one object: a policy boundary (the remediation level governs every member) and an access boundary (only assigned identities manage members). Semi remediation was chosen because this tenant's only endpoint is also its detection-test rig - Full could quarantine a test artifact before it is observed; No-automated-response would also drop the device from automatic attack disruption. Semi keeps response capability and preserves evidence. Membership propagation measured: Apply at 06:11, committed by 06:39 - under 28 minutes, at or under the vendor's 30-60 minute window. The finding with consequences: for the whole propagation window the device was NOT in this group. It sat in "Ungrouped devices (default)", which runs FULL remediation - the opposite of the Semi chosen here. The rule previewed as matching instantly while committed membership lagged, so every visible signal said "configured" while the effect (and the intended remediation level) was not yet in force. POS-011's family, sharpest instance: the fallback does not do nothing, it does the specific thing the design chose to avoid. Do not test against a device until membership commits, not merely until the rule previews. Scoped delegation composed across models: the analyst identity (POS-027, Unified RBAC per POS-026, unlicensed) gained scoped visibility of the device as a member of this group, via an Entra security group bound to the legacy device group. That composition was the lab's open prediction and it resolved yes. The exclusive half of scoped access - analyst DENIED a device outside the group - is un-runnable with one device and is the reason this entry stays revisit:true. A scope that has never excluded anything has not been shown to scope. Needs a second, deliberately out-of-group device to close.

### Lab 06

| ID | Setting | Location | State | Kind | Revisit | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POS-031` | Attack Surface Reduction rules | `Set via PowerShell Add-MpPreference on the device; viewed at security.microsoft.com > Reports > Attack surface reduction rules` | Two rules set to Block - WMI event-subscription persistence, and process creation via PSExec/WMI. Both enforcing and confirmed firing. | hardened | yes | 2026-07-19 |
| `POS-041` | Enforcement scope (MDE security settings management) | `Defender portal > Settings > Endpoints > Configuration management > Enforcement scope` | Off - 'Use MDE to enforce security configuration settings from Intune' disabled. Observed 2026-07-27, not changed. | default | yes | 2026-07-27 |

**`POS-031` — Attack Surface Reduction rules.** Two rules configured, both Block, and demonstrated firing in both audit and block states on one rule with an identical benign trigger (a WMI process create). Audit: action allowed, silent, local event 1122, cloud ActionType ...Audited. Block: action refused, user notification, event 1121, ...Blocked. Both events coexist in one query, distinguishable only by the ID / suffix - the trap the tooling invites. The headline finding: the Defender ASR report shows this device as "Rules off" - 0 in block, 0 in audit, 18 turned off - while both rules were actively blocking. The Detections view showed 0 with all filters set to Any. Advanced hunting, the device timeline, and the local event log all carried the events. Cause is scope, not lag - CONFIRMED 2026-07-27. The ASR REPORT is built around policy-managed (Intune/MDM) rules; rules set locally via Add-MpPreference enforce on the endpoint but are invisible to THAT REPORT's configuration and detection views. An analyst trusting the dashboard would read the box as unprotected and re-deploy while protection runs. AMENDED 2026-07-27 - "invisible to the console" was too broad and is disproved by counterexample. Microsoft Secure Score is a Defender console, names Defender for Endpoint as its product, and shows BOTH rules Completed at 9/9 points. Its history recorded the transition: each rule logged at 0/9 "has become relevant" on 2026-07-18 and 9/9 "points gained by completing ... Great work!" on 2026-07-19, the day Lab 06 was built. Tamper Protection did the same, 0/8 to 8/8. That transition also settles scope-vs-lag BY ELIMINATION rather than by the two verifications previously pending: if the configuration had never reached the Defender cloud, Secure Score could not have logged it changing. The corrected finding is stronger than the original - not one console blind to a local rule, but TWO CONSOLES IN THE SAME PRODUCT READING THE SAME CONFIGURATION AND DISAGREEING COMPLETELY, one reporting 18 rules off and zero in block while the other awards full points and timestamps the moment they were set. An analyst cannot tell which is right without going to the endpoint. Caveat: Secure Score read Completed on 2026-07-27 with both VMs deallocated, so it reports last-known configuration, not live state. This is a direct downstream consequence of POS-022. Because Intune enrolment never fires, local PowerShell is the only available way to set ASR here - and that is precisely the path the reporting UI cannot see. A Lab 01 defect silently governs the visibility of every ASR rule set in Lab 06. Secondary: ASR blocks are recorded as telemetry, not raised as alerts. Neither event reached Incidents & Alerts. A successful block is treated as resolved, so ASR visibility requires hunting or the ASR report - never the alert queue. Two PowerShell literacy traps recorded in configuration-inventory.md: Get- MpPreference does not return ASR rules in entry order (positional pairing required, or Block reads as Audit); and Add-MpPreference appends while Set- MpPreference replaces. End state both Block; either rule can be set to AuditMode later - noted so the register and the device stay in sync. Preconditions from earlier labs: AV Normal mode (POS-029/Lab 03) makes rules enforce; Semi remediation (POS-030) kept the block from being auto-quarantined mid-test.

**`POS-041` — Enforcement scope (MDE security settings management).** Discovered 2026-07-27 while reviewing Settings > Endpoints during module 55. Read-only; the toggle was NOT changed. MDE security settings management lets Defender for Endpoint enforce security configuration on devices that are, in the portal's own words, "not yet enrolled to Intune". It requires a matching switch in Intune's Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector settings - the same connector page that carries POS-011's Windows compliance toggle. Both are off. WHY IT MATTERS - it corrects an asserted absence in Lab 06. That lab's design table states that Intune needs an enrolled device (POS-022, enrolment never fires), GPO needs AD, and therefore "PowerShell is the only available path". That was asserted, not checked. This is a second path, and it exists specifically for the unenrolled case this tenant is in. The door was closed, not absent - and nobody tried the handle. The consequence runs deeper than a rationale. Had this been on, the two ASR rules could have been deployed as POLICY-MANAGED rather than local, which is exactly the class the ASR report can see. POS-031 - the most consequential finding in this repository - describes a report blind to locally-set rules. That finding is real and stands, but it exists because of a switch that was off and openable, not because of a foreclosure. A different starting configuration would have produced a different lab and no finding at all. NOT TESTED, deliberately. Enabling it buys nothing until there is an endpoint to enforce against - both VMs are deallocated - and it would put an unexercised change into this register. It is also two switches, not one, the second being on the POS-011 connector page. Deferred to the batched session that also covers custom detections and analytics rules, where a live endpoint is needed anyway. When it is tested, it is a DIRECT TEST OF POS-031's MECHANISM: deploy the same two rules as policy and see whether the ASR report begins showing them. Success moves "the report is scoped to policy-managed rules" from well- supported inference to demonstrated fact. Predict before testing: policy- managed ASR may conflict with the locally-set rules already on the box, and that interaction should be reasoned about in advance rather than discovered. Adjacent observation, same settings area: Intune Permissions is empty - no Entra groups have ever been granted Endpoint Security permissions in Intune. Consistent with the rest of the Intune-side foreclosure and recorded so the absence is on the record as observed rather than assumed.

### Lab 07

| ID | Setting | Location | State | Kind | Revisit | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POS-033` | Windows Security Events ingestion via Azure Monitor Agent | `Azure > Monitor > Data Collection Rules (dcr-winsec-lab); VM LAB-SRV-DEFENDER-01 > Extensions (AzureMonitorWindowsAgent)` | DCR dcr-winsec-lab collecting Common-tier Windows Security events from LAB-SRV-DEFENDER-01 into the SecurityEvent table. AMA auto-installed via the DCR association. Pipeline verified with live telemetry. | hardened | yes | 2026-07-25 |

**`POS-033` — Windows Security Events ingestion via Azure Monitor Agent.** The first agent-based ingestion in the project. Distinct from POS-032's connector path: this is the Azure Monitor Agent collecting a machine's own Windows Security log via a Data Collection Rule, landing in the billed SecurityEvent table. AMA auto-installs when the DCR is associated to the VM (installed in under 5 minutes). SCAgentChannel reads Direct - the per-machine path, not WEF/WEC. Data lands in SecurityEvent, not WindowsEvent. Cost decision - Common tier, not All. The Windows Security log is high-volume and SecurityEvent bills fully here: the 500 MB/day/server free allowance exists only under Defender for Servers Plan 2, which this environment does not have (Defender for Cloud declined at Lab 04). So the DCR tier is the only cost control, and Common (curated security IDs) was chosen over All (the firehose). This is the DCR-as-cost-lever principle in its most consequential form. Four findings recorded in Lab 07. (1) Direct-AMA path confirmed via SCAgentChannel Direct, landing in SecurityEvent; the WindowsEvent/WEF half is documented but not observed (no collector topology). (2) Hostname truncation: the Azure name LAB-SRV-DEFENDER-01 (19 chars) exceeds the 15-char Windows NetBIOS limit, so the Computer field reads LAB-SRV-DEFENDE - an exact-match filter on the full name returns nothing. (3) Machine-context events: WORKGROUP\ account, AccountType Machine, confirming the VM is WORKGROUP-joined (no AD, consistent with the Entra-only environment). (4) 4624 does not mean a human logged in: on a VM started but never signed into, the only successful logons were 2x LogonType 5 (service, SYSTEM), zero interactive (the Type 2 query returned empty) - the meaning is in LogonType, not the raw 4624 count. VM deployed cost-safe: Standard_D2s_v3 (smallest available), smalldisk image, Standard HDD, Security type Standard (POS-018 parity), inbound None, no public IP (dissociated and deleted), Bastion-as-labadmin access, auto-shutdown 23:00 Pacific, Manual patching, boot diagnostics off. Access posture is deliberately BETTER than VM 1: inbound None and no public IP, versus VM 1's internet-facing RDP (POS-019). Standing cost note: Bastion bills more than the VM while running - AMENDED 2026-08-12, this holds for the Basic SKU deployed here and NOT for Developer, which emitted no meter row at all across the subscription's full usage history (POS-099) - a per-session teardown decision. Deferred: Endpoint Threat Protection Essentials (the SecurityEvent analytics rules) did not auto-install with the Windows Security Events solution, contrary to source guidance - ingestion does not need it; detection on this data is deferred to the alerts/incidents work later in the course.

**`POS-034` — Entra ID and Azure Activity connectors.** The two foundational first-party connectors - control-plane (AzureActivity) and identity (SigninLogs/AuditLogs/risk). Both were installed as Content Hub solutions earlier; this records the configuration that made them flow, and the verification by querying tables rather than trusting the connector status label ("connected is not flowing"). Connector-tiers model (the analysis grounding Labs 04/07/08): config effort scales with how foreign the source is to Sentinel. Defender XDR (Lab 04) is the same platform - auto-connected. AMA/Windows events (Lab 07) is your resource on an external disk - agent + DCR. Azure Activity and Entra ID (this lab) are separate Azure/Entra services with their own logging systems - connecting them means reconfiguring THOSE services to export (a diagnostic setting or policy), plus licensing. This is why these two surface the "connected is not flowing" warning: the connector page reads connected while the real work sits on the source service. Azure Activity - Method A failed, Method B worked, and B was the right choice. The Azure Policy wizard (Method A, the guide's recommended path) failed TWICE: "you need to log in" at submission, with Policy > Assignments confirming 0 policy assignments both times. Not user error - the wizard's managed-identity creation needs a privileged token and the session kept expiring. The manual diagnostic setting (Method B) succeeded first try. Analysis: for a SINGLE subscription, Method B is architecturally appropriate, not a fallback; Method A's machinery (policy + managed identity + remediation + enforcement) only earns its complexity at multi-subscription scale. Decision rule: count subscriptions. CORRECTED 2026-07-26 - SigninLogs vs EntraIdSignInEvents. This entry originally recorded the two as the same sign-in data under two schema names, one per query surface. That was inference, and it was wrong. Running the identical "search * | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | summarize count() by $table" on both portals on 2026-07-26 returned BOTH tables in the Defender result (SigninLogs 6, EntraIdSignInEvents 972) and ONLY SigninLogs in the Azure/Log Analytics result. Two names for one dataset cannot resolve side by side in one query and disagree about how many rows exist. They have different PRODUCERS, not different names. SigninLogs and AuditLogs are workspace tables written by the Entra diagnostic setting, scoped by the four log types selected here (interactive sign-ins only), and billable. EntraIdSignInEvents, EntraIdSpnSignInEvents, GraphAPIAuditEvents, EmailEvents, EmailUrlInfo and IdentityInfo are Defender XDR lake tables, written by XDR independently of this connector, and free. The decisive evidence was already in this lab and went unread: the XDR tables carry service-principal and Graph activity, which are exactly the high-volume log types this connector DECLINED, so they cannot be connector-fed. The original empty SigninLogs is explained by the Entra propagation lag (~10-15 min) that this same entry documents two paragraphs down - the correct explanation was sitting beside the wrong one. The store-partition method (the finding that replaces the one above). Running one identical search * table census on both portals and diffing the two table lists cleanly separates the free Defender XDR lake from the billable Log Analytics workspace: what appears in the Azure run is workspace-resident and meterable, what drops out is XDR-native and free. Measured 2026-07-26 - workspace: SecurityEvent, Heartbeat, Usage, AzureActivity, SigninLogs. XDR-only: GraphAPIAuditEvents (3578 events, the volume that prompted the check and bills nothing), EntraIdSignInEvents, EntraIdSpnSignInEvents, EmailEvents, EmailUrlInfo, IdentityInfo. The method is free, repeatable, and answers a cost question by measurement instead of inference. IdentityInfo landing XDR-side also establishes that it is not evidence of UEBA running in this workspace - worth knowing before the behavioural-analytics section rather than after. Query kept at kql/sentinel/store-partition-diff.kql. Timestamp trap, sixth occurrence - and the cleanest measurement of it. The two exports of the same rows disagreed by exactly 7 hours across three tables (SecurityEvent, Heartbeat, AzureActivity), matching to the second: the Defender export rendered local time, the Azure export rendered UTC and labelled its column "Latest [UTC]" where the Defender export left it unlabelled. That column header is a free tell. Prior occurrences were two different events compared across surfaces; this one is the same rows exported twice, so the offset is measured rather than inferred. Licensing test PASSED - conclusion unchanged, evidence corrected. Entra sign-in ingestion needs P1/P2 and the E5 trial's P2 is live. The 489 EntraIdSignInEvents originally cited as proof establishes nothing about this connector, being XDR-native and present regardless of it. The actual proof is SigninLogs populated in the WORKSPACE - 7 events, latest 2026-07-26 21:56 UTC, that last one being the operator's own sign-in to the Azure portal minutes earlier, which also demonstrates the interactive-only scope working as selected. The risk tables (AADRiskyUsers/AADUserRiskEvents) may stay empty even when licensed - they populate only on actual risk detection, and a quiet lab tenant produces none; empty risk tables are not a licensing failure. AuditLogs was selected but absent from a 24h window on 2026-07-26; a quiet tenant with no directory changes was the likely reason, recorded as unconfirmed rather than assumed. CLOSED 2026-07-29: AuditLogs carries data. The connector was fine and the tenant was quiet, which is what the entry declined to assume at the time. Both connectors are platform diagnostic settings - VM-independent - so they keep ingesting with the VM and Bastion deallocated. Cost: low lab volume; the section's two ingestion levers (connectors coarse on/off, DCRs fine filter-at-source) are the disciplines already applied in Labs 07-08. Measured billable surface as of 2026-07-26 is five tables and negligible volume against the 10 GB/day trial allowance.

**`POS-044` — Microsoft Sentinel UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics).** Enabled 2026-07-28 19:58 local (02:58 UTC) at Defender > System > Settings > Microsoft Sentinel > UEBA. Microsoft Entra ID directory sync on; Active Directory left off (it needs Defender for Identity and on-prem AD, neither of which exists here). Seven data sources connected. Behaviors layer - a separate tab, enabled independently, creating SentinelBehaviorInfo and SentinelBehaviorEntities - deliberately left OFF to keep one variable. THE COST FINDING, MEASURED RATHER THAN QUOTED. Microsoft Learn states that no licence is required and there is no extra cost for UEBA, but that it generates new data in new workspace tables and additional storage charges therefore apply. Both halves are true and only the first is memorable. IdentityInfo now appears as a BILLABLE DataType at 0.001416 MB/24h, alongside SigninLogs (0.038757) and AuditLogs (0.003583). Total billable volume 0.0437 MB/day against a 10 GB/day allowance. The principle is proven; the bill is not. "The feature is free" and "enabling it is free" are different claims. THE STORE-PARTITION METHOD DETECTED A TABLE CHANGING SIDES. On 2026-07-26 IdentityInfo appeared in the Defender census and NOT in the Azure one - XDR- only, which was the evidence used at the time to conclude UEBA was not running. It is now workspace-resident with four rows. The method built during the Lab 08 correction did exactly what it was built for, on a question it was not built for. PREDICTION 2 OF 4, recorded before the fact. Predicted that BehaviorAnalytics, IdentityInfo, UserPeerAnalytics and UserAccessAnalytics would cross to the workspace side. IdentityInfo (4 rows) and BehaviorAnalytics (1 row) appeared; UserPeerAnalytics and UserAccessAnalytics did not. HYPOTHESIS, NOT ESTABLISHED: a three-identity tenant has no peer groups to compare against and almost no access history, so those two may be structurally unpopulatable here rather than merely slow. The competing explanation is ordinary latency - Learn mentions a 14-day resync cycle - and a single census cannot separate them. INITIAL SYNC TOOK UNDER AN HOUR, NOT "A FEW DAYS". Enabled 02:58 UTC; IdentityInfo carries data at 03:50 UTC. Learn's estimate is presumably written for organisations with thousands of identities; for three it is off by roughly two orders of magnitude. AzureActivity independently corroborates the enablement, recording control-plane writes at 03:08 UTC. BehaviorAnalytics INHERITS THE SOURCE EVENT'S TIMESTAMP. Its only row reads 13:25:48.657 UTC - identical to the millisecond to the latest SigninLogs row. The behaviour record carries the time of the underlying activity, not the time UEBA produced it. Consequence for hunting: UEBA's own processing latency cannot be measured from TimeGenerated, and a BehaviorAnalytics row tells you when something happened, not when it was noticed. ENABLING UEBA IS THREE ACTS, AND THE PAGE REPORTS "ENABLED" AFTER THE FIRST. Feature toggle, then directory sync, then data source connection. With the toggle on and nothing else done, both directory services read "Sync disabled" and the source list read "0 sources" - the feature switched on and analysing nothing. Only the empty-state text ("Start sync for at least one directory to see the available data sources") reveals the required order. Configured is not effective, in a feature whose own status page says otherwise. "CONNECT AVAILABLE DATA SOURCES" CONNECTS EVERYTHING ELIGIBLE, AND ELIGIBLE MEANS THE CONNECTOR EXISTS. Seven sources went green; THREE carry data. AAD Managed Identity SignIn Logs and AAD Service Principal SignIn Logs are connected to log types deliberately declined in Lab 08 (POS-034) - green because the Entra connector exists, empty because its log types were refused. Security Events names the LEGACY AGENT connector, where Lab 07 built ingestion via AMA and a DCR. Device Logon Events needs a running device and both VMs are deallocated. Four sources will read Connected indefinitely and contribute nothing, and nothing on the page distinguishes them from the three that work. The bulk action was taken rather than the curated three, and is recorded as CHOSEN rather than defaulted - it is also the path the portal labels Recommended settings, and therefore the realistic one. Reverting three sources afterwards would have produced a half-corrected state harder to describe honestly than one clean decision. The data source list is a CATALOGUE, NOT AN INVENTORY. AWS CloudTrail, GCP Audit Logs and Okta are listed and greyed out with "Data source is not ingested to Sentinel" plus a Content Hub link. It shows the feature's reach independently of this tenant, which is better design than hiding them. PREREQUISITE CLAIM CORRECTED. Microsoft Learn lists Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at workspace scope and Log Analytics Contributor at resource- group scope - Azure RBAC - and this project asserted on that basis that Global Administrator alone would not suffice. The portal's own banner reads "Only a Global Administrator or a Security Administrator in your Microsoft Entra ID can turn this feature on or off", an Entra role, and the enable succeeded. Documentation and portal name different requirements; the portal was right about what the portal enforces. WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW: UEBA's actual value. Fifteen days of tenant life, three identities and almost no activity cannot produce a behavioural baseline, and anomaly detection without a baseline detects nothing. This was designed as a PLUMBING TEST from the outset - does enabling it create the tables, does the data cross to the billable side, how long does sync take - and must not be read as an evaluation of UEBA.
