**`POS-099` — Azure Bastion Developer SKU billing, measured by meter emission rather than by amount.** P89-10 is CONFIRMED, and in a stronger form than it was predicted. The prediction was that the Developer SKU bills 0 USD. What the export shows is that it emits nothing to bill. The distinction is only available because the same export contains a positive control for zero-priced metering. Sentinel writes daily rows - Free Trial Analysis from 07-25 and Free Benefit - M365 Defender Analysis from 07-26 - at CostUSD 0, every day, without interruption. So the pipeline demonstrably records services that are metered and priced to zero. Bastion is not in that category. Two different zeros in one file: a measured zero and an absent row. This is the two-read rule applied to a cost surface. The billing-account scope was read first and returned "No cost reported during this period" for the whole of August - a false empty caused by scope, not by spend (divergence row 203). Had the Bastion conclusion been drawn there, it would have been drawn from a surface that was reporting nothing about anything. Bounded deliberately: this says the Developer SKU produced no meter rows for one host, created and deleted inside a single day, on a pay-as-you-go subscription. It does not establish that Bastion never bills, and it does not extend to the Basic or Standard SKUs, which are documented as hourly and were the reason Lab 21's host was deleted rather than stopped.

**`POS-095` — Unified audit log retrieval - the read side of the ingestion enabled in Lab 09.** Closes a loop open for sixteen days. Three separate figures in this job were unpopulated rather than empty and could each have been misread as an answer: Total results 0 while Queued, a header reading 2 items beside a single row on first read, and a mid-run count of 8 at 77.78 percent that finished at 19. Progress rendered exactly 7/9, so the job steps a fixed unit count rather than estimating - the mid-run figure is not proportional and is not a partial answer. Search-UnifiedAuditLog returned 21 rows for identical scope against the portal's 19. Diffed rather than estimated: the export is a strict subset and both extras are second occurrences of timestamps already present, confirmed by identical Identity at two ResultIndex positions with ResultCount 21. Nineteen distinct records, two emitted twice, no error and no warning. Not testable in this tenant: every record-retention figure in MOD-92. Sixteen days of history cannot test 180 days, one year or ten. Recorded as documented, never as measured.

**`POS-096` — eDiscovery Manager role group membership, and the eDiscovery access boundary.** This is MOD-92's licensing trap on a second axis. Premium audit events are generated for a user only after the licence is assigned to that account; content-search access exists only after the role group is assigned. Entitlement is not assignment, twice, in consecutive modules. The refusal rendered TWO stacked modals. On top, a Client Error reading only "Missing required permissions to view case". Beneath it, a Permission Error carrying the cause and the remedy in full. The useless one renders first, so a user who dismisses it and navigates away never sees the actionable one. Page chrome rendered fully behind both - Case settings, Process manager, Summarize this case, and the descriptive text - while every data-bearing element was withheld. Stated precisely: case-scoped action buttons render without the case being readable.

**`POS-097` — Temporary eDiscovery Manager grant and its revocation - measured before, during and after.** configured != effective on the REVOCATION side, which is the more dangerous direction. An administrator would remove the role, verify it on exactly the surfaces built for that question, and reasonably conclude the boundary had closed. Three role surfaces agreed it had. The service disagreed and only a write attempt exposed it. Two claims made during the lab were falsified here and are recorded rather than removed. First, that the case pre-existed and was merely invisible - a blank Created column was read as evidence, and Case settings disproved it. Second, that persisting access was explained by a direct case membership materialised on first access - the Permissions page did list that membership, and the backend refused a write on the grounds that it did not exist. The persistence was a stale client view over a service that had already revoked. The refused write surfaced a raw .NET exception type and a case GUID directly in a customer-facing dialog, under the same generic Client Error title used for the unrelated refusal in POS-096. The diagnostic payload offered behind that dialog was not captured and is not reproducible from this identity now that access has closed. revisit true - the grant/revoke cycle should be re-measured if any eDiscovery role is ever assigned again, and the Content Search case and LAB-EDISC-MOD94-A search remain in the tenant, inaccessible to admin.

**`POS-098` — Optical character recognition, and what content search indexes.** Two findings, opposite directions, one search. Text was extracted from image pixels on a path that neither visible OCR setting governs. A prediction that the image would be missed because OCR applies only after review-set collection was FALSIFIED; a reviewer had flagged that pre-explanation as improper before the test ran. The unindexed file is the sharper result. Three surfaces reported no gap: absent from results, Partially indexed items 0 (0 B), and Matches from advanced indexing 0 (0 B). The advanced-indexing pass demonstrably ran - the card set changed and the run took roughly six minutes against one - and found nothing. Extension-based exclusion sits outside the partially-indexed model entirely, so it is not a gap the tooling is built to report and no amount of opting in reveals it. The gap surface is also off by default. Include partially indexed items ships unchecked, and checking it reveals two further nested options - one of them advanced indexing - plus a third-level runtime warning. The advanced-indexing control cannot be discovered without first checking a box that is off. Why the .labx is excluded - extension, content sniffing, or indexer policy - is NOT established. Only that it is. revisit true.
